body:
incident-bot: Pager: KV cache fragmentation rate spike detected on prod-gpu-pool-7. Metric: kv_alloc_fragmentation_ratio > 0.55 for 3 mins. Possible allocator thrashing / PyTorch CudaMalloc churn. Auto-annotated by anomaly-detector.

jamie (oncall): taking this. seeing increased 5xx and latency spikes on text-generation endpoints. running smoke tests.

sasha: copied. I see long tail latency in the trace view, lots of small allocations then spikes of CUDA OOM in logs. Repro on canary?

kevin: quick check — did we roll any batch or kv changes in the last deploy window?

maya: yes, there was a small change to continuous-batching heuristics yesterday (commit 3a4f8c2) that raised max_batch_bytes for long-seq requests.

jamie (oncall): ok possible root. customer impact: two customers reporting sustained 95p latency increases and one internal smoke test hitting 500s. tagging acme-corp and medflow.

ops-runbook-bot: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) reduce continuous_batching.max_bytes to previous value, 2) enable arena compaction ramp, 3) trigger a rolling restart for affected pool.

jamie (oncall): attempting quick config rollback on pool-7 now.

kevin: handoff incoming — i'm remote but can execute hotfix. jamie, if you confirm, i'll push a config and watch allocs.

jamie (oncall): confirm. run the hotfix and post commands.

kevin: running patch:
```bash
# revert continuous-batching max_bytes to safe default
rdctl config set runtime.kv.continuous_batching.max_bytes 262144
rdctl config set runtime.kv.allocator.arena_compact_threshold 0.05
rdctl rollout restart pool prod-gpu-pool-7 --grace 30s
```

kevin: applied, starting rolling restart. watching metrics.

sasha: logs from node gpu-07: `RuntimeWarning: CUDA malloc failed: out of memory` dropping after restart sequence began.

maya: I can see fragmentation_ratio trending down from 0.62 -> 0.28 over the last 90s. Latency 95p dropping from 1.8s -> 720ms.

jamie (oncall): customer-facing status: "We're aware of increased latency for model endpoints in region us-west-2. We rolled a mitigation and are monitoring. No data loss. Updates every 15m."

kevin: temporary mitigation worked. Next steps: revert the batching heuristic commit from yesterday and schedule a safer canary for the change. We should also add a runtime guard to avoid increasing max_bytes when fragmentation_ratio > 0.4.

maya: agreed. I'm opening an incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime to own allocator follow-up. ticket: IRT-4792.

jamie (oncall): handing off to kevin for longer-lived fixes — I'm pausing on-call for 10m while I triage alerts. kevin, please ack and own the post-incident runbook.

kevin: ack. I'll take ownership. plan: 1) revert commit 3a4f8c2 (hotfix PR pending), 2) add an automated rollback threshold, 3) add an arena compaction schedule and add unit test for compaction heuristics.

ops-runbook-bot: recommended post-incident tasks: add alert on fragmentation_ratio > 0.45, add a smoke test for high-seq workloads to CI, and document the allocator tuning knobs in runbook.

maya: customer impact note for postmortem: 2 paying customers impacted, brief latency degradation at 95p for ~12m, no token loss, 1 internal smoke failing.

jamie (oncall): adding reminder: tag support and SRE for follow-up. I'll post timeline in incidents channel after we finish hotfix PR.

kevin: creating PR to revert the change now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1209

sasha: thanks team. once PR merges we'll schedule a careful canary with increased observability.

incident-bot: Incident updated to "mitigated". Severity downgraded to Sev3 while we validate postmortem action items.

kevin: postmortem owner: eng-runtime (kevin). ETA on draft: EOD.

maya: noted. pinging account reps for ACME and MedFlow.

jamie (oncall): closing handoff. I'll re-open if anything flares. Good job everyone :thumbsup:
